PullRequest.Title: Fix Windows separators in bundled source-map URLs
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Normalize relative output paths before constructing CDN source-map URLs in the current esbuild bundle path. On Windows, nested paths from `path.relative` contain backslashes; the same value was interpolated into both JavaScript and CSS `sourceMappingURL` comments.

- Extract the existing comment rewrite into a small helper and normalize path separators to `/`.
- Preserve POSIX paths, root-level output, no-CDN behavior, and the existing JS/CSS regexes and comment formats.
- Add portable `path.win32`/`path.posix` regression cases plus small in-memory minified esbuild bundles. Assertions compare complete emitted strings, not URL-parser normalization.
- Update the build notes. No changes to mappings, source contents, Unicode enforcement, or other build transforms.

## Validation

- Confirmed the nested Windows regression fails for both JS and CSS before separator normalization.
- `node --test .\build\next\test\source-map-url.test.ts` - 15 tests passed.
- `npm --prefix .\build run typecheck` - passed.
- `node .\build\hygiene.ts .\build\next\index.ts .\build\next\source-map-url.ts .\build\next\test\source-map-url.test.ts .\.github\instructions\buildNext.instructions.md` - passed, including formatting and ESLint for all three changed TypeScript files.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` - passed.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: A caller starts one Node bundle process; all regular esbuild entry-point builds complete, bootstrap entries complete, then each emitted JS/CSS output is post-processed and written. rewriteSourceMappingURL remains on the per-output serialized post-processing path immediately before writeFile, but performs the same two whole-content regex replacements as before plus a short relative-path separator normalization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn the Node build/next/index.ts bundle command
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One process per invoked bundle target
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same caller spawned the same single bundle process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The process must finish before packaging continues; its placement and count are unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Clean/create output directories, read build date and tslib, create output directories, and write every emitted file/map
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Reads are bounded setup operations; mkdir/write operations scale with emitted outputs and are executed serially in post-processing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same directories were created and the same outputs were written with the same serialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations remain on the bundle critical path; the helper runs before the existing write but adds no filesystem call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One helper call per emitted JS/CSS file after code splitting; effective cardinality is the number of emitted code/style outputs, not source modules. Each regex pass scales with that output's content length; path normalization scales only with the short relative path.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Regular entry points are bundled with Promise.all; bootstrap entries and the subsequent output-file post-processing/write loop are serial. The diff does not alter either concurrency pattern or introduce a burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no cache for source-map rewriting because each emitted file has distinct content and path. Cold and warm bundle behavior are equivalent for this helper; esbuild-internal caching is not relied upon. The diff does not change cache keys, coalescing, or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed hunk and full bundle loop directly establish one call per emitted JS/CSS file, unchanged regex count, unchanged writes, and unchanged scheduling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact output count and bundle sizes vary by target, but the only new enabled-CDN work is replaceAll over a short path plus function-call overhead; it does not change the dominant content scans or I/O.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff preserves the existing O(total emitted JS/CSS bytes) rewrite and output I/O, adding only O(total relative-path characters) separator normalization required by the fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Bundle without --source-map-base-url, including local development bundle invocations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After esbuild completes, each emitted JS/CSS output reaches path.relative, enters rewriteSourceMappingURL, immediately returns the original string, and is written. Before the diff, this branch skipped path.relative and the helper call entirely.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create output directories and write emitted files/maps
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One mkdir attempt and one write per emitted output, unchanged from the base revision.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical per-output mkdir/write behavior, with source-map replacement skipped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing serialized filesystem work dominates this path; the diff does not add or move an I/O boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The newly executed path.relative/helper guard occurs once per emitted JS/CSS output and scales with short path length; it does not scan or copy file contents when the URL option is absent.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Output processing and writes remain serial; no queue, limiter, or fan-out changed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved or useful for distinct output paths. Cold and warm behavior are the same, and the early return preserves the original content object.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the helper's explicit early return and changed call site prove the exact added work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Target-dependent output cardinality is not needed to assess the mechanism: each new operation is bounded to path parsing and a guard, with no content traversal or allocation proportional to bundle bytes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Although the diff newly computes path.relative and calls the guard when CDN rewriting is disabled, this bounded path-only work is negligible beside unchanged bundling and per-file filesystem I/O.

Scenarios.Scenario: Running the build/next Node test suite
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new test file executes pure helper assertions and two tiny in-memory esbuild builds for one-line JS/CSS inputs; those builds must complete before the test file passes, but write:false keeps generated outputs out of the filesystem.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke esbuild.build with bundle and linked source maps for one-line JS and CSS inputs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly two calls per execution of this test file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This test file and its two tiny esbuild calls did not exist; the neighboring source-map test suite already used esbuild independently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Introduced on the test-only critical path; both calls must finish before their assertions complete, but they do not affect product startup or packaging output.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed test matrix: twelve pure Windows/POSIX/root/nested option cases, two in-memory esbuild builds, and one missing-comment case. Input sizes and build count are constant rather than repository-sized.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The test code contains no Promise.all or explicit concurrency; the two esbuild tests are individually awaited under node:test scheduling. There is no unbounded fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Helper cases have no cache. Any esbuild service reuse is implementation-dependent and not required for the verdict; cold execution is still bounded to two minimal builds.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added tests directly show two awaited write:false builds and fixed input sizes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native esbuild service startup/reuse is not visible in repository code, but cardinality and input size are fixed, so uncertainty cannot produce scaling or retention risk.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The new test cost is bounded to two minimal in-memory builds and introduces no repository-sized work, filesystem output, retention, or concurrency burst.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and every diff page. Traced CDN and no-CDN bundle paths plus the new tests, including subprocess/filesystem boundaries, effective output cardinality, serialization, and cache behavior. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced, and the PR is a correctness fix rather than a concrete performance-regression fix.
